answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from requiring each identity to maintain a continuously updated computational atlas of peer attestations that must be refreshed at every network summit. Generating and verifying this atlas demands sustained GPU cycles that grow linearly with the number of fake identities an attacker controls. The attacker cannot simply whisper false claims into the system because each atlas update is cross-checked against the public ledger, forcing the attacker to burn real electricity and hardware depreciation for every additional Sybil they wish to sustain.
